title: History survives removal; enrolling again anchors from last completion
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. Seed a maintenance schedule (standard steps):
  3. ↳ In Settings > Maintenance click New schedule; the "Untitled schedule" editor opens.
  4. ↳ Inline-edit the title to a test name (e.g. "Highway Tractor PM").
  5. ↳ Click Add service, give it a name (e.g. "PM-A") and a calendar interval (e.g. Every 3 months), and save the service.
  6. ↳ Click Save on the schedule.
  7. Enrol an asset (standard steps):
  8. ↳ Open Customers, open a test customer (e.g. "Aacrest Works"), open its Assets tab and open an asset (e.g. unit 402 · 2019 Freightliner Cascadia).
  9. ↳ Open the asset's Maintenance tab (the last tab, after Notes) and click Enroll in Schedule.
  10. ↳ Pick the schedule (e.g. "Highway Tractor PM"), leave the last service dates blank unless the case says otherwise, and click Enroll.
  11. On the asset's Maintenance tab, PM-A row menu > Mark complete > Completed elsewhere, Reset date 1 Sep 2026 > confirm (this records a completion).
custom_steps:
1. On the Maintenance tab open the schedule menu > Remove from schedule and confirm.
  2. Click Enroll in Schedule, pick "Highway Tractor PM" and read PM-A's last service date; click Enroll.
  3. Read PM-A's Due cell.
  4. Archive the schedule in Settings, restore it, enrol the asset again and read PM-A's last service date.
  5. In Settings add a new service "CVIP" (compliance, Term 12 months) to "Highway Tractor PM" and save; reopen the enrolled asset's Maintenance tab.
  6. On the asset's Maintenance tab open the schedule menu and hover the (i) beside Remove from schedule.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The asset leaves the schedule; its completion is kept.
  • PM-A's last service date is pre-filled with 1 Sep 2026 (the last completion of a same-named service).
  • PM-A comes due 3 months after 1 Sep 2026 (Dec 2026).
  • After archive and restore, enrolling again pre-fills 1 Sep 2026 again: archiving removed the enrolment, not the history.
  • The enrolled asset does not get the new CVIP service, and nothing warns about it: the shop must enrol the asset again to get it.
  • On the design the (i) reads "Removing a schedule and adding another keeps every cycle: the new schedule's services anchor from the last completion of a matching service where one exists, otherwise from now."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10563 (S6, Edit and archive a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S6 (What survives; S6-E1, S6-E2, S6-E4); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard M1; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-E1: “Removing a schedule from an asset does not destroy history. Cycles belong to the asset and service pair”
  • S6-E2: “Applying a new schedule afterwards anchors each service from the last completion of the service of the same name on that asset, otherwise from now”
  • S2-R14: “A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month, counted from the last completion”
  • S6-E4: “Archiving unenrolls without destroying history. Each asset keeps its completed cycles per S6-E1, so enrolling it again later anchors from the last completion per S6-E2”
  • S6-E3: “A new regulatory requirement is the known weak point. The shop must apply the schedule again per unit and nothing warns it”
  • Design board, artboard M1 (schedule header (i)): “Removing a schedule and adding another keeps every cycle: the new schedule's services anchor from the last completion of a matching service where one exists, otherwise from now.”
